- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong lag in correcting downward trends; if true price drops >2% from prior, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lagged decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model overfits recent volatility; use 14-day EWMA or sentiment-weighted average to smooth out noise and avoid overreaction to short-term sentiment swings.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward bias if price has been above 30-day moving average for >5 days.
